reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the well-established effect of W addition on thermal stability and glass-forming ability from Fe-P-based amorphous systems (P43, P31) to the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-P high-entropy alloy, without providing a new mechanism or resolving a conflict between passages. The proposed mechanism (negative mixing enthalpy, size mismatch, increased viscosity) is a textbook concept (P9, P12) and is stated almost verbatim from P43. The predicted outcome (increased Tx, wider supercooled liquid region) is the same as that reported for W additions in other systems (P43, P44). The idea is a straightforward substitution of one element into a known alloy, which is a minor variation on existing work.
